headline: Congress used a disapproval resolution to nullify an FCC rule that would have set new customer privacy and data security requirements for broadband and telecommunications providers.
what_it_does: This joint resolution cancels a Federal Communications Commission rule published in December 2016 that would have applied the Communications Act's customer privacy rules to broadband internet access and other telecommunications services. The rule would have required providers to tell customers about opt-in and opt-out choices for sharing their information, set data security and breach notice duties, and barred service deals that required giving up privacy rights. Because the resolution nullifies the rule, those requirements do not take effect.

who_it_affects.how: They are not required to follow the FCC's privacy, opt-in/opt-out, data security, and breach notification rules that the nullified rule would have imposed.
They are not subject to the new customer consent and disclosure requirements that the FCC rule would have applied to them.
The new FCC privacy protections, including required consent choices and breach notices, will not apply to their service providers under this rule.

when_it_takes_effect: The resolution took effect when it was signed into law on April 3, 2017, which nullified the FCC rule.
